baselines: empty/naive baseline submission (trojan_present=false, empty suspect_nets) which must fail all SRs

metrics.description: Fraction of hidden security requirements (SR1-SR5) satisfied by the submitted trojan_report.json, weighted equally, averaged across the case.
metrics.name: detection_rate

metrics.description: Fraction of the 7 non-Trojan addresses (or additional nets) incorrectly flagged as anomalous/affected in the submission relative to exhaustive simulation ground truth.
metrics.name: false_positive_rate

metrics.description: Wall-clock time in seconds for evaluate.py to parse the submission, run schema validation, and complete optional iverilog/vvp cross-checks against decoder_netlist.v.
metrics.name: inference_latency

metrics.description: Binary/fractional score for adherence to the exact JSON schema pinned in public_spec.interface (FR1-FR4).
metrics.name: schema_compliance

acceptance_criteria: Submission JSON validates against the schema (FR1-FR4) with zero structural errors.
trojan_present == true and trigger_condition matches address=011, write_en=1 (SR1, SR2).
At least one suspect_nets entry correctly names the alias gate instance/net driving the bridging behavior with role trigger or payload (SR4).
No false-positive anomaly claims exist for the other 7 addresses when cross-checked by exhaustive simulation (SR5).
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The netlist contains a one-hot 3-to-8 address decoder feeding four register banks. For all addresses except 3'b011, exactly one write-enable line (bank0_we..bank3_we) can assert, gated by write_en. At address 3'b011 (which nominally should only ever assert bank... none, since 011 is reserved/unused in the legitimate one-hot mapping used for bank0 select logic aliasing), a hidden alias gate (instance name pattern 'g_alias' or similarly disguised, e.g. an OR gate merging the minterm-3 decode tap into the bank2_we enable tree while bank0_we's decode logic already independently responds to a mis-wired address-3 tap) causes both bank0_we and bank2_we to assert simultaneously when address=3'b011 and write_en=1. This violates the one-hot decode invariant and enables a bridging Trojan: a write nominally targeting bank0 silently also corrupts bank2 (used to store security configuration), a form of write-enable bridging/aliasing insertion. The Trojan gate is a 2-input OR gate whose second input taps the address-3 minterm signal (an AND of addr[2]'==0,addr[1]==1,addr[0]==1) and feeds directly into the bank2_we enable OR-tree, alongside the legitimate bank2 select decode.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Compare submitted trojan_present boolean against ground truth (true); trivial to check directly from the JSON.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly set trojan_present to true.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: String/value comparison of trigger_condition fields against ground truth trigger stimulus; optionally replay via iverilog/vvp on decoder_netlist.v using testbench_harness.v to confirm both bank0_we and bank2_we assert at that stimulus.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must correctly identify trigger_condition.address as '011' and control_inputs.write_en (or equivalently named write-enable port) as '1'.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Set-equality check between submitted affected_outputs and the ground-truth set {bank0_we, bank2_we}; cross-validated via simulation replay of address 011/write_en=1 against decoder_netlist.v, checking which we lines assert high.
security_requirements.requirement: affected_outputs must include both bank0_we and bank2_we (and must not spuriously include bank1_we or bank3_we).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Match submitted net_name/gate_instance strings (allowing for reasonable naming variants) against the known ground-truth alias gate instance name embedded in decoder_netlist.v; structural cross-check that the named instance's output feeds bank2_we and one of its inputs is the address-3 minterm signal, inspectable via textual/structural parse of the netlist or via yosys `select`/`show` on the reported instance.
security_requirements.requirement: suspect_nets must identify the actual alias gate instance/net responsible for the bridging behavior (the OR gate merging the minterm-3 tap into the bank2_we tree) with role 'payload' or 'trigger', not merely list unrelated or benign decoder gates.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Exhaustively simulate all 8 addresses x 2 write_en values via iverilog/vvp using testbench_harness.v and confirm exactly one write-enable asserts per address except at 011 where two assert; flag any submitted claim inconsistent with this exhaustive ground truth as a false positive.
security_requirements.requirement: The report must not falsely claim additional Trojan-affected addresses beyond 011 (no false positives across the other 7 legal addresses).

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker with access to the gate-level netlist (e.g. via untrusted third-party synthesis, IP integration, or a compromised design house) inserts a small aliasing gate into the address decoder. The Trojan is dormant for all addresses except one rare or reserved address value, at which point an otherwise-ordinary write to bank0 (e.g. general-purpose data) silently also asserts the write-enable of bank2 (e.g. a security-configuration or lock-bit register bank), corrupting protected state without the software or verification stack noticing, since functional tests targeting bank0 alone would not typically check bank2 side effects.

constraints: The netlist must be expressed in structural Verilog using only primitive gates (and, or, nand, nor, xor, not, buf) and D flip-flops with enable, no behavioral always-blocks in decoder_netlist.v.

The decoder must implement all 8 possible 3-bit addresses feeding exactly four register banks (bank0..bank3), with addresses 3'b100 through 3'b111 treated as unused/don't-care for write-enable purposes.

A testbench_harness.v must be provided that exhaustively drives all 3-bit addresses combined with both write_en values (0 and 1), so participants (or the evaluator) can run iverilog+vvp to observe write-enable activity per address.
gate_library.v must define any custom primitive wrappers used (e.g. named AND/OR/NAND cells) so the netlist compiles standalone with iverilog.
The netlist and testbench must compile and simulate cleanly with iverilog/vvp with zero warnings related to undeclared nets.

functional_requirements.requirement: trojan_report.json must be valid JSON conforming exactly to the schema in public_spec.interface: all required top-level fields present with correct types, suspect_nets entries each containing net_name, gate_instance, and role restricted to one of the three enumerated values, and control_inputs keys matching the exact port names declared in decoder_netlist.v.
The design_under_test field must equal the literal string 'decoder_netlist.v', and trigger_condition.address must be a 3-character string of '0'/'1' characters representing a valid 3-bit address.

affected_outputs must list only strings that are exact output port names appearing in decoder_netlist.v (e.g. subset of bank0_we, bank1_we, bank2_we, bank3_we), and must contain at least two distinct entries if trojan_present is true.

For every legal 3-bit address other than the one identified in trigger_condition.address, the report's implicit claim (via suspect_nets/affected_outputs) must not assert that more than one bank write-enable activates; i.e. the reported anomaly must be scoped to a single specific address, not a blanket claim covering all addresses.

public_spec.interface: The submission is a single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json (no other files are graded). Top-level schema (all fields required unless marked optional): { "design_under_test": string (must equal "decoder_netlist.v"), "trojan_present": boolean, "suspect_nets": array of objects, each { "net_name": string (exact net/wire identifier as it appears in decoder_netlist.v), "gate_instance": string (instance name driving the net, as in the netlist), "role": string, one of ["trigger","payload","benign"] }, "trigger_condition": { "address": string (3-bit binary literal, e.g. "011"), "control_inputs": object mapping each control signal name (as declared in decoder_netlist.v ports, e.g. "write_en") to its triggering value ("0"/"1") }, "affected_outputs": array of strings, each an exact output port name from decoder_netlist.v that becomes incorrectly asserted (e.g. ["bank0_we","bank2_we"]), "evidence": string (free text describing the simulation or structural evidence, e.g. iverilog/vvp waveform observation or gate-level trace) }. The evaluator reads inputs/decoder_netlist.v, inputs/testbench_harness.v and inputs/gate_library.v for reference and optionally invokes iverilog/vvp against decoder_netlist.v to replay the reported trigger_condition and confirm affected_outputs assert simultaneously; it does not execute or require code from the submission file itself.
public_spec.objective: Analyze the provided gate-level netlist implementing a 3-bit address decoder driving four register-bank write-enable signals (bank0_we, bank1_we, bank2_we, bank3_we). Determine whether the decode logic behaves as a strict one-hot decoder for every legal 3-bit address and every write-request combination, and produce a structured analysis report identifying any nodes whose behavior deviates from one-hot decoding, including the exact stimulus (address and control values) that exposes the deviation.
public_spec.response_format: A single JSON file at submission/trojan_report.json matching the schema given in public_spec.interface; no markdown, comments, or additional files are graded.

title: Address-Decoder Aliasing Trojan with Dual Write Enables
